tax: Flugabgabe (Flugabgabegesetz FlugAbgG, Art. 57 Budgetbegleitgesetz 2011, BGBl. I Nr. 111/2010)
announcement_event: End of the federal government budget retreat (Regierungsklausur) in Loipersdorf; Chancellor Faymann and Finance Minister Pröll present the 2011 budget package including a new Flugticketabgabe
ticket_cutoff_rule: Tickets bought on or before 2010-12-31 exempt. FlugAbgG s.16(2): tax arises only if the contract (Rechtsgeschäft) was concluded after 2010-12-31 and the departure is after 2011-03-31. Departures with no underlying contract taxed from 2011-04-01.
source_quote: "von der neuen Flugticketabgabe (100 Millionen Euro)" (Bundespressedienst, 23.10.2010) | "20.12.2010 Beschluss im Nationalrat" | "Ausgegeben am 30. Dezember 2010" | s.16(2) "wenn das Rechtsgeschäft nach dem 31. Dezember 2010 abgeschlossen worden ist und der Abflug nach dem 31. März 2011 erfolgt"
source_type: Official press release (Bundespressedienst, Federal Chancellery, via APA-OTS); parliamentary record (Parlament.gv.at); legal gazette (BGBl. I, authentic RIS PDF via Wayback capture)
notes: Announcement: OTS0073 timestamped 23.10.2010 17:45 says the government agreed the budget 'heute nach der Regierungsklausur im steirischen Loipersdorf'; ÖVP release OTS0067 (23.10.2010 17:31) also lists 'einer Flugticketabgabe'; earliest OTS item naming the levy is a Niki Lauda reaction (OTS0057, 23.10.2010 15:52). OTS archive search 2010-06-01 to 2010-10-23 for Flugticketabgabe/Flugticket/Flugabgabe/Ticketsteuer found nothing before 23 Oct; OTS items of 22 Oct 2010 describe the retreat as ongoing and do not mention the levy. Newspaper leaks outside OTS not checked. Later steps: Ministerialentwurf 234/ME (AbgÄG part of BBG 2011-2014) received 2010-11-03, consultation to 2010-11-17; Regierungsvorlage 981 d.B. 2010-11-30 (budget speech same day); Nationalrat 2nd and 3rd reading 2010-12-20 (SPÖ, ÖVP for); Bundesrat no objection 2010-12-23. s.16(2) text identical in RV 981 d.B., Nationalrat decision 332/BNR and BGBl. Live RIS site blocked by a bot check, so BGBl read from Wayback copy of the RIS authentic PDF.

tax: Air Passenger Duty rate doubling (Finance Act 2007 c.11 s.12, amending FA 1994 s.30)
announcement_event: Pre-Budget Report 2006 statement by Chancellor Gordon Brown to the House of Commons
ticket_cutoff_rule: No purchase-date exemption in the statute. FA 2007 s.12(4): amendments apply to any carriage of a passenger beginning on or after 2007-02-01 (keyed on flight date only; no grandfathering clause for tickets sold earlier).
source_quote: "From 1 February, we will double air passenger duty." (HC Deb 6 Dec 2006, col. 310) | s.12(4) "have effect in relation to any carriage of a passenger on an aircraft which begins on or after 1st February 2007" | Act dated "[19th July 2007]"
source_type: Parliamentary record (Hansard, House of Commons); legislation (legislation.gov.uk)
notes: Hansard col. 310 continues: for most journeys (over 75 per cent) duty rises from GBP 5 to GBP 10. enactment_date = Royal Assent of Finance Act 2007 (19 July 2007); the new rates applied from 2007-02-01, before Royal Assent. s.12(5) defers payment of any increase falling in an accounting period ending before 2007-03-21 to the first accounting period ending after that day. The date and text of any provisional-collection (Ways and Means) resolution were not checked. publication_date left blank: a UK Act has no separate gazette publication. The HM Treasury PBR 2006 document itself was not read; the Hansard statement is the primary record of the announcement.

tax: Air Travel Tax (Finance (No. 2) Act 2008 s.55; Air Travel Tax Regulations 2009, S.I. No. 134 of 2009)
announcement_event: Budget 2009 Financial Statement by Minister for Finance Brian Lenihan in Dáil Éireann
ticket_cutoff_rule: No purchase-date exemption: tax applied to all departures on or after 2009-03-30 'irrespective of when a passenger booked or paid for the flight' (Revenue ATT Manual). s.55(2)(a) charges every departure on or after 30 March 2009.
source_quote: "I intend to introduce an air travel tax from 30 March 2009; the tax will apply to all departures from Irish airports." (Financial Statement, 14 October 2008) | Act dated "[24th December, 2008]" | "irrespective of when a passenger booked or paid for the flight" (Revenue ATT Manual)
source_type: Department of Finance budget statement (budget.gov.ie, archived copy); legislation (Irish Statute Book); Revenue Commissioners manual
notes: Financial Statement header reads 'Mr Brian Lenihan, T.D. 14 October 2008'. Announced rates: EUR 10 per passenger, EUR 2 on journeys under 300 km. Design changed between announcement and law: the Budget summary exempted airports with fewer than 10,000 departing passengers in the previous year, while the Revenue manual describes the enacted threshold as 50,000. enactment_date = date of the Finance (No. 2) Act 2008. publication_date left blank: Iris Oifigiúil notice and S.I. 134/2009 dates not checked. Oireachtas debates site returned a CAPTCHA and was not used; budget.gov.ie now redirects to gov.ie, so the archived official page was read.

tax: Passenger departure tax increase Lm10 to Lm20 (Airport (Passenger Service Charge) (Amendment) Regulations 2005, L.N. 60 of 2005, amending L.N. 118 of 1997)
announcement_event: Budget 2005 speech by Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Lawrence Gonzi in Parliament
ticket_cutoff_rule: No purchase-date exemption stated. L.N. 60/2005 raises the fee payable by the aircraft operator per departing passenger embarking, from 2005-08-01. Budget speech: increase applies to every trip starting from Malta; existing exemptions kept (day passengers, incoming passengers returning home); sea travel not increased.
source_quote: "As from 1st August, this passenger departure tax will increase to Lm20 for every trip starting from Malta." (Budget Speech 2005, p.53) | "Today, 24th November 2004, the Honourable Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Dr Lawrence Gonzi, presents the Budget for 2005." (Ministry of Finance) | "Suppliment tal-Gazzetta tal-Gvern ta’ Malta, Nru. 17,739, 11 ta’ Marzu, 2005"
source_type: Ministry of Finance budget page and official budget speech (mfin.gov.mt, archived copy); legal gazette (Legal Notice, legislation.mt)
notes: Speech section 'Increase in the passenger departure tax on trips starting from Malta' describes the then Lm10 tax as collected by airlines from passengers starting their journey in Malta. Speech PDF does not print its delivery date; the date comes from the Ministry of Finance Budget 2005 page (Wayback capture 2004-11-28). Gazette date read from the Maltese-language version of L.N. 60/2005 (page B 685); the English page (B 686) carries no date. enactment_date left blank: the Legal Notice does not state a date of making. Note the 4.5-month gap between Gazette publication (2005-03-11) and entry into force (2005-08-01). Parliament of Malta sitting records not checked.

announcement_event: Federal cabinet retreat (Kabinettsklausur) of 6-7 June 2010 adopts the savings package (Zukunftspaket / Eckpunkte for the 2011 budget and 2014 financial plan); results published 7 June 2010
ticket_cutoff_rule: Bookings made before 2010-09-01 exempt: tax applies to all bookings made from 2010-09-01 with departure from 2011-01-01 (s.19(1) LuftVStG as summarised in BT-Drs. 17/10225).
source_quote: "Sie erhebt eine nationale ökologische Luftverkehrsabgabe für alle Passagiere, die Einnahmen von jährlich 1 Milliarde Euro bringen soll." (Bundesregierung, Mo, 07.06.2010) | "Kabinettklausur am 6. und 7. Juni 2010" (BT-Drs. 17/3030)
source_type: Official government web article (bundesregierung.de, archived copy); Bundestag printed papers (Drucksachen 17/3030 and 17/10225)
notes: Confirms 7 June 2010 as the public announcement: the Bundesregierung page dated So, 06.06.2010 only previews the two-day retreat and does not mention aviation; the 07.06.2010 pages carry the decision. Cabinet adopted the HBeglG 2011 bill incl. LuftVStG on 2010-09-01; Bundestag passed it 2010-10-28; LuftVStG dated 2010-12-09, BGBl. I S. 1885 of 2010-12-14, in force 2010-12-15 (all per BT-Drs. 17/10225). BT-Drs. 17/10225 also notes early-booking (Vorzieh) effects from trips booked before 2010-09-01. Germany was an optional check; bill and gazette dates are as reported in BT-Drs. 17/10225 rather than read from BGBl directly.
